newsitem.title: USA: Accused CIA shooter challenges death penalty law.
newsitem.headline: Accused CIA shooter challenges death penalty law.

text.p: A lawyer for a Pakistani man accused of killing two CIA workers and wounding three others in a 1993 shooting spree near the spy agency's headquarters Wednesday challenged the use of the death penalty in the case.

Public defender Richard Goemann, representing the accused shooter, Mir Aimal Kansi, filed a motion seeking to declare the Virginia death penalty law unconstitutional and to bar imposition of the death penalty in the case.
He also asked the judge in Fairfax County, Virginia who has been presiding over the case to dismiss the murder charges that carry the death penalty.
Kansi, 33, was apprehended in Pakistan by FBI agents and brought back to the United States last month. He is scheduled to go on trial in November on murder and other criminal charges.

Among his arguments, Goemann claimed the Virginia death penalty law violates the constitutional protection against cruel and unusual punishment, fails to provide meaningful guidance to the jury and violates due-process guarantees.
"The Virginia capital murder and death penalty provisions are unconstitutional under both the U.S. and Virginia Constitutions," said in the 54-page court filing.
The prosecutor has vowed to seek the death penalty if Kansi is convicted. A hearing on the death penalty motion and other issues is expected early next month.
